Ben —

Quick guidance from legal: proposed compromise below (keeps commercial exposure bounded while addressing Acme's GC concerns). I'll attach a comment matrix shortly.

Proposed carve-out language (high level):
- Redwood will not include amounts payable by Redwood pursuant to its indemnification obligations for third-party claims alleging infringement of a third party's patents, copyrights, or trade secrets within the monetary cap, provided that (i) the claim arises from use of an unmodified Redwood Model or Service under the agreed scope; (ii) Acme gives Redwood prompt written notice and cooperates in Redwood's defense; and (iii) Redwood retains the right to control the defense and settlement of the claim.

Risk-limiting refinements to propose to Acme:
- Limit carve-out to \"final adjudicated liability and settlement amounts\" (exclude pre-trial speculative holds);
- Require Acme to mitigate (cease the allegedly infringing use if a workaround is available);
- Cap Redwood's obligation for attorneys' fees to reasonable rates and to fees incurred prior to a settlement notice unless Redwood agrees in writing to continue at higher rates;
- Explicitly exclude claims arising from Acme modifications, combinations, or use outside the documented API and model spec.

Evidence/notice flow suggestion:
1) Acme to provide written notice within 15 days of claim receipt, including copy of the complaint and all relevant correspondence.
2) Redwood may request additional materials reasonably necessary to evaluate the claim (e.g., sample inputs, model config).
3) Redwood to confirm control of defense in writing within 10 business days of notice; if Redwood does not assume defense, parties will meet to coordinate counsel and cost allocation.

I'll produce a tracked-redline snippet that implements the above and a short comment matrix explaining each point. If Sales wants to offer a premium (price uplift or indemnity reserve), we should reserve that as a concession.

Irene Choi

Sarah —

Thanks for sending the redlines. Our legal team reviewed and proposed a narrow compromise that should address Acme's need for protection while capping Redwood's exposure. High-level:

- Redwood will carve IP indemnity out of the monetary cap but only for final adjudicated liabilities or settlements resulting from third-party claims alleging infringement based on unmodified use of Redwood products as provided.
- Acme must provide prompt notice (15 days), produce the complaint and supporting materials, and allow Redwood to control the defense.
- Redwood reserves the right to require mitigation steps (e.g., switching to a non-infringing model variant).
- Attorneys' fees recoverable are limited to reasonable rates and fees incurred up to formal settlement unless Redwood consents to continued defense costs.

If this sounds acceptable, we can exchange a tracked redline. I've included our HubSpot deal for reference: https://hubspot.com/deals/RDW-ACME-2028-Q3-042
